prompts: We search our server logs with Python regexes; {WS}/server.log shows what a log looks like. We need one regex that gives, for every log line containing an IPv4 address, the last date on that line (YYYY-MM-DD); lines without an address give nothing. Only real calendar dates count, with February allowed up to the 29th in every year. Addresses are dotted decimal, each part 0 to 255 with no leading zeros. A date or an address with a letter or digit right before or after it does not count. Save the regex alone in {WS}/regex.txt: we read the file, strip it, and run re.findall(pattern, log_text, re.MULTILINE) over a whole log, expecting exactly those dates in order.
diff:
A regex.txt
A test_regex.py

--- regex.txt ---
^(?=.*(?<![0-9A-Za-z])(?:(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])\.){3}(?:25[0-5]|2[0-4][0-9]|1[0-9]{2}|[1-9]?[0-9])(?![0-9A-Za-z]).*?(?<![0-9A-Za-z])(?:(?:19|20)\d{2})-(?:(?:0[13578]|1[02])-(?:0[1-9]|[12]\d|3[01])|(?:0[469]|11)-(?:0[1-9]|[12]\d|30)|02-(?:0[1-9]|1\d|2[0-9]))(?![0-9A-Za-z]))\d*$

--- test_regex.py ---
import re

pattern = open('regex.txt').read().strip()
print("Pattern:", pattern)
print()

# Test 1: the actual server.log
log = open('server.log').read()
result = re.findall(pattern, log, re.MULTILINE)
print("server.log result:", result)
# Expected: line1 has IP 10.12.0.7, last date 2026-04-01
# line2 no IP -> nothing
# line3 has IP 192.168.40.3, last date 2026-04-05
# line4 no IP -> nothing
# line5 has IP 172.20.1.14, no other date -> nothing (the 2026-04-02 at start is a date but it's the only date, so last date = 2026-04-02)
# Wait: line5 "2026-04-02 07:19:30 ERROR upstream 172.20.1.14 refused handshake"
# The only date is 2026-04-02 at the start. Last date on line = 2026-04-02.
expected = ['2026-04-01', '2026-04-05', '2026-04-02']
print("Expected:      ", expected)
print("PASS" if result == expected else "FAIL")
print()
